signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Tokyo CPI Repricing
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags JPY as the week's dominant leader at +1.134% across 7 pairs, while AUD sits as the sole laggard at −0.817% across 4 pairs, creating an extreme bilateral spread of 1.950%. Spot AUD/JPY trades at 109.46, pressured after September Tokyo Core CPI printed hot at 2.7% year-on-year against 1.9% expected, forcing a repricing of BoJ policy tightening expectations. This nominal outperformance directly defies the +335bp policy rate carry advantage favoring AUD from RBA at 4.6% vs BoJ at 1.25% (OIS differential +337bp). A MOVE index reading of 108.1 signals elevated bond market volatility that continues to encourage rapid carry de-risking into JPY. AUD/USD trading below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6933 confirms broader Australian dollar technical deterioration. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY; bond market volatility and Tokyo inflation repricing outweigh carry support. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 30 Oct — hold market bias priced. Risk: Broad cross-asset risk-on rally resumes and suppresses bond volatility, reasserting the 335bp carry advantage.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Tokyo CPI
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.81, holding below its SMA50 at 158.15 and SMA200 at 158.48 while remaining above the SMA20 at 156.18. The 25-delta risk reversal sits at −2.60 vol, showing an aggressive put skew where the options market prices premium downside protection despite a +275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%). Tokyo Core CPI accelerated to 2.7% versus 2.4% projected, reinforcing front-end rate support for the yen and prompting Asian official commentary on yield volatility. Meanwhile, USD/JPY 1M ATM implied volatility trades at 9.2% against 30-day realized volatility of 9.8%, yielding a negative volatility risk premium of −0.7% that indicates option pricing complacency ahead of high-impact US macro prints. CFTC data shows JPY leveraged funds net long +4,472 contracts at the 98th percentile of the 52-week range (z = +2.66), reflecting institutional positioning crowded in favor of yen strength. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, downside protection demand dominates into technical resistance. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 12:30 UTC — forecast 52K. Risk: US NFP delivers a major upside beat, lifting US yields and forcing a squeeze back through the SMA200 at 158.48.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Rates Divergence + Elevated Volatility Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1252, down 1.08% over the past week and positioned below its SMA20 (1.1482), SMA50 (1.1532), and SMA200 (1.1615). The policy rate differential of Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% delivers a +135bp carry advantage favoring USD (+146bp via OIS), while Germany-US 2-year yield spreads widened 43bp in USD's favor over the past five sessions to −182bp. US 5-year yields widened 23bp over 5 sessions to 5.06% (FRED, as of Sep 29) led by a 21bp rise in real yields. Options markets display elevated stress with EUR/USD 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.5% against 30-day realized volatility of 3.8%, generating a +2.7% volatility risk premium alongside a 25-delta risk reversal put skew of −1.01. Retail positioning is heavily skewed long at 88%, contradicting institutional leveraged fund positioning which holds net short −58,805 contracts. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; real yield expansion and structural carry deficit cap spot upside. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI y/y at 09:00 UTC — forecast 3.0%. Risk: Eurozone headline inflation prints significantly above forecast, forcing hawkish ECB repricing ahead of the October 29 meeting.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Carry Compression + Hedging Demand
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3211, testing below its SMA20 (1.3383) and converging SMA50/SMA200 cluster at 1.3455/1.3447. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds cut net long exposure by 12,179 contracts WoW to +6,519, sitting at the 8th percentile of its 52-week range (z = −1.66) and marking rapid institutional liquidation. The policy spread of Fed 4.00% vs BoE 3.75% provides a +25bp carry advantage to USD (+17bp in OIS space), amplified by UK-US 2Y yield spreads moving 31bp in USD's favor over five sessions to −24bp. The options market reflects heightened protection costs, with 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.6% versus realized volatility of 4.2%, creating an elevated volatility risk premium of +2.4% alongside a 25-delta risk reversal put skew of −1.01. This combination confirms institutional hedging against further Cable downside rather than buying into trend dips. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; institutional positioning liquidation and yield spread compression leave spot vulnerable. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 12:30 UTC — forecast 52K. Risk: BoE policy repricing turns aggressively hawkish following upcoming UK housing data, driving a recovery back above the SMA20 at 1.3383.
